learning_objectives.description: Describe the meaning of a limit; evaluate one-sided and two-sided limits of a function from its graph or a table of values and vice versa; evaluate two-sided limits via the respective one-sided limits; decide when a limit equals infinity or -infinity and interpret such infinite limits.

definitions.definition_plain: We write “the limit as x approaches a of f(x) equals L” and say “the limit as x approaches a of f(x) exists and is equal to L” provided we can make f(x) as close to L as we like by choosing x to be as close to a as needed, without ever actually reaching or equaling a.
definitions.definition_latex: We write $\displaystyle \lim_{x\to a} f(x) = L$ and say ``the limit as $x$ approaches $a$ of $f(x)$ exists and is equal to $L$'' provided we can make $f(x)$ as close to $L$ as we like by choosing $x$ to be as close to $a$ as needed without ever actually reaching/equalling $a$.
